# abadia64ks, H3: the game's data blocks (hand-written source of the C64 memory map; c64/NOTAS_MAPA.md).
# One row per block of the CPC 64 KiB memory the game needs on the C64 (the graphics come from
# data/c64graf/graficos64.tsv, written by tools/c64_graficos.py).  mapa64.py places
# them (-> mapa64.tsv, mapa64.inc); inventario64.py adds what the sessions measured
# (-> data/datos64_inventario.tsv); punteros64.py finds the pointer fields inside them (-> punteros64.tsv).
# columns: name, CPC start (hex, '-' = a C64-only block), length (bytes, decimal), kind, zone, mode, align, desc
#   kind: var (variables, the initial value matters), smc (an operand or opcode of the Z80 code that the code
#         rewrites: a variable on the C64), tabla (constant table), regs (record array, variable), texto,
#         buffer (scratch: no initial value), conv (converted to a C64 format)
#   zone: zp ($24-$FF), var ($0200-$07FF), datos (packed below $C000), hueco (the bitmap's invisible cells),
#         c4 ($C400-$CFFF), io ($D000-$DFFF, read and written with the I/O switched off), a fixed C64
#         address $xxxx, or sigue (right after the previous row's block: one contiguous region)
#   mode (hybrid check, juego/m6502/sombra6502.c): copia = copied CPC -> 6502 before a call and compared
#         after (pointer fields relocated, punteros64.tsv); conv = C64-format constant taken from the data
#         image, neither copied nor compared; nada = neither (C64-format buffers, init-only data)
#   align: 1, or 256 for a page-aligned table
# ---- zero page: the operands the Z80 code rewrites (its fastest variables) ----
